essays.title: Psychosis: first episode and predisposing factors

sections.title: Introduction
sections.intent: The argument in two sentences, and the scope of the essay.

sections.title: What psychosis is, and the continuum
sections.intent: Definition first, with its source named, then the transdiagnostic continuum that lets risk be discussed below the diagnostic threshold. Merged, because separately they were two descriptive sections.

sections.title: The prodrome and the first episode
sections.intent: The window in which onset happens, and what subthreshold symptoms predict.

sections.title: Predisposing factors
sections.intent: Neurodevelopmental, behavioural and environmental. The title promises this section, so it carries the most weight and the largest budget.

sections.title: Assessing risk, and what the instruments cannot say
sections.intent: The PQ-B and its kind. A screening threshold is not a clinical determination.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.intent: What this evidence base cannot establish. Mostly design: no longitudinal data.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.intent: What follows, and the handover to Essay 2.

essays.title: Vignette: internet and AI use as a precipitating factor

sections.title: Introduction
sections.intent: The argument in two sentences.

sections.title: The vignette
sections.intent: The case the essay argues from. Composite, and labelled as such.

sections.title: Naming it, and the scale of exposure
sections.intent: Define the term, say whose definition it is and that it is descriptive rather than diagnostic; establish the exposure is population-level. Merged.

sections.title: This is not new: pathoplastic, not pathogenic
sections.intent: The intellectual core. Influencing machines since 1810. Concede this before claiming anything, then ask whether this technology differs.

sections.title: Why this technology invites it
sections.intent: What is actually different: a fluent, agreeable, second-person interlocutor.

sections.title: What the evidence actually shows
sections.intent: Survey base rates, then the clinical tail, with the cross-sectional limit in the authors' own words.

sections.title: Formulation and holistic treatment plan
sections.intent: The 5Ps formulation of the vignette, with each factor meeting the intervention that targets it: predisposing, precipitating, perpetuating, protective and presenting. Absorbs assessment and the digital-use history as its opening step, CBTp and coping as its interventions, and the access-and-companionship evidence as protective factors where the evidence supports reading it that way. "Holistic" is testable here: does the plan touch every P?

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.intent: What the evidence can and cannot support, and what would settle it.
